findings.justification: This regex is a test assertion over a fixed malicious MIME fixture, not an HTML sanitizer or security allowlist. It verifies that untrusted source remains available or that collected plain text lacks the known fixture tag; production rich-text sanitation is not implemented by this assertion.

This SHA-256 is the retry-domain digest of org, actor/client identifiers and an idempotency key. Authenticator return-object taint is propagated into public identity fields; no password verifier is derived or stored. Existing persisted idempotency identities must remain unchanged.

This SHA-256 creates a deterministic write request UUID from actor identity, declared tool key and canonical input, not a password verifier. Duplicate recovery separately checks org/user/principal, complete input/declaration digests and immutable target; reads use randomUUID. The full target fence is pinned below.

This hash derives document-action identity/preview idempotency from actor identifiers and exact document preview data. It does not store or authenticate a user password; broad authenticator-object taint reaches actor IDs. Changing it would change persisted retry identities rather than improve password storage.

These hashes index server-generated OAuth codes/access/refresh tokens created by randomToken using randomBytes(32), not low-entropy user passwords. Token lookup still checks authorization scope, expiry and revocation. SHA-256 for uniformly random 256-bit bearer tokens does not require a password KDF.

This is HMAC-SHA256 with the receipt signing key over a canonical audit payload, not password storage. Actor metadata from authentication is receipt data. Slow/salted password hashing would destroy deterministic receipt verification; the signing domain and keyed construction remain unchanged.

This SHA-256 fingerprints canonical import/preview JSON, including actor identifiers, rather than deriving a password verifier. Authentication-return taint reaches identity fields, but the digest is used for exact review/idempotency matching and grants no authority.

Only org ID, owner ID, provider and provider-subject identity are hashed into the retained principal digest. OAuth binding validation taints the whole record; actual access/refresh credentials are not hash inputs. The digest is an immutable account-identity fence, not password storage.

oauthDigest derives scoped account/storage identity and client-policy fingerprints. validateOAuthBinding contains only public binding metadata; oauthClientFingerprint explicitly omits client_secret. This is not a password verifier and cannot be changed without breaking retained account keys; caller inputs are pinned below.

The target is the exact Host-created opaque srcdoc iframe (allow-scripts without allow-same-origin), fixed canonical trusted script and escaped Host-origin metadata. Exact contentWindow/null-origin readiness plus current identity/authority gate one scoped MessagePort; stop revokes/removes only that frame. Global parent worker-src self/blob is explicit for SPA inheritance; child hash-only script CSP and connect-none confine the inherited Blob Worker. Author bytes never execute in the parent or document. Wildcard targets the opaque frame, not an arbitrary window; all supporting source is pinned. Persistent consent parsing changes only explicitly reviewed grant deadlines: null requires the literal until_revoked mode. Frame identity, opaque origin, finite Experience lease, one-port transfer and revocation gates remain unchanged.

The flagged includes call compares complete elements of a normalized scope array, not substrings of a URL. Scope values are tokenized/allowlisted by normalizeOAuthScopes and persisted scope arrays are checked by oauth-account. A foreign URL containing the literal does not equal an array element.

The flagged includes call compares exact scope-array elements. The preceding guard rejects non-arrays and invalid elements. It is not URL substring sanitization; prefixed/suffixed URLs do not authorize an operation. The existing reduced-scope contract remains enforced.

This regex is an assertion over a fixed returned OAuth fixture URL, not the authorization-origin allowlist. Production connection begin parses URL and requires exact reviewed origin and callback state; the current production flow source is pinned below. Persistent durable scope parsing does not loosen OAuth navigation: Begin and callback deadlines remain finite, and exact parsed authorization origin plus a single exact callback-state parameter are still required.
